R4-V (prefix h8) is finished. The deliverable is `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h8_board_entry.md`, with VERIFY REQUEST blocks, exact rerun commands, negatives, a size-gating table and a "not done" list. No `src/*.rs`, `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` changes. Unpatched A/B runs used a private workspace copy under `nm-target-r8/unpatched_ws`.

Other files, all under `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\`:
- Code: `src/bin/h8_vectors.rs`, `src/bin/h8_common/`
- Proposals: `results/h8_proposed_patch.md` (Q1-Q7)
- Tables: `results/h8_*.json`, `results/h8_*.md`, `results/h8_*.log`
- Run scripts: `results/h8_run_all.sh`, `results/h8_run_part2.sh` ... `results/h8_run_part5.sh`
- Report scripts: `results/h8_report*.py`

**Caveat:** everything is synthetic or templated-corpus data, and the box was loaded for part of the run (load probe stored in each JSON). `h8_hnsw_confirm_*` latencies are unusable (box 3-4x slow); the headline latencies come from the `lat2` mode. That mode uses 3 builds, interleaved kernels, and p99 of the per-query minimum over 7 passes.

**1. Fixed-crate HNSW sweep (3 datasets, 1 thread)**
- Recall now saturates at 1.000, and the hnsw_rs floor ef=10 is the knee.
- Recall@10 >= 0.99 at p99 120-180 µs (p50 65-97 µs) at 5.9-8.8 KB/vec:
  - MiniLM N=23k: M24/efc100/ef16 gives recall 0.993, p99 121 µs.
  - BGE-768 N=23k: M32/efc200/ef10 gives 0.994, p99 145 µs.
  - Synthetic N=30k: M16/efc200/ef16 gives 0.996, p99 180 µs.
  - g15, unpatched on a loaded box, needed 0.23-0.5 ms for the same target.
- Best recall at a fixed p99 budget:

  | p99 budget | MiniLM | BGE-768 | Synthetic N=30k |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | <=150 µs | 0.996 | 0.994 | 0.969 |
  | <=200 µs | 0.998 | 0.999 | 0.998 |
- The AVX2 dot kernel is still worth taking: paired p50 ratio 0.82-0.92 (median ~0.87), recall unchanged.

**2. Self-recall check (items not their own top-1, k=10, every item queried)**
- Patched crate at ef=512: 0 of 20-30k items lost on synthetic and MiniLM for every efc > 2M config tested (3 builds each).
- The same code on the unpatched registry crate loses 0.4-1.7 % of items.
- Residual on real BGE at efc100 is 0.04-0.08 % (16-19 and 8-9 of 23,453). It is 0 at efc200.
- New trap, independent of the patch: efc <= 2M leaves up to 42 % of items unreachable even at ef=512. It is worst at efc=2M, e.g. M48/efc96 loses 33-42 % on synthetic. I propose clamping efc >= 3M.

**3. Flat vs HNSW crossover and why R3 differed**
- d=384: exact flat ties HNSW up to N~5k (77 µs vs 56-76 µs). HNSW is 2.5-3.4x faster at 10k, 7-10x at 30k and 7-18x at 1e5, at recall >= 0.99.
- d=128: flat wins to ~10-15k.
- "Flat fastest at 30k" is a misreading of H2. H2's actual numbers say HNSW was 1.3-2.5x faster at ef 32-128 (d=128, N=30k). I reproduced them: flat 341 µs (H2 said 340), and HNSW 2.4-2.6x / 1.5x / 0.9-1.07x faster at ef 32/64/128.
- R3 and I measure at the ef floor (10-16), where HNSW is 4-6x (d=128) to 7-10x (d=384) faster.
- On the unpatched crate, M16 cannot reach 0.99 recall at all; at the 0.99 target the fix makes M32 HNSW 1.1-1.8x faster.
- I found no thread effect.

**4. N=3e5 recall with larger M (3 builds each)**
- M16/efc200 stays at 0.76-0.89 for ef 32-256, with or without the patch.
- M32/efc100 reaches 0.964 at ef128 and 0.993 at ef256.
- M48/efc100 reaches 0.986 at ef128 and 0.996 at ef256 (p99 1.2-1.7 ms, 7.3 KB/vec).
- Larger M fixes it; the patch alone does not (worth at most +0.06 recall at 3e5).
- R3's single-build 0.84-0.92 for M16 was not reproduced.
- HNSW at 1e6 was skipped (6-7 GB projected against the 2.5 GB cap).

**5. Max vectors per GB, counting-allocator heap (B/vec; M vectors/GB)**

| Config | B/vec | M vec/GB |
|---|---|---|
| turbovec 2-bit | 100 | 9.96 |
| turbovec 3-bit | 196 | 5.1 |
| turbovec 4-bit | 196 | 5.1 |
| int8 flat | 388 | 2.58 |
| block-fp16 flat (exact) | 816 | 1.23 |
| f32 flat | 1536 | 0.65 |
| HNSW | 5.1-8.7 KB | 0.11-0.2 |

- turbovec 3-bit is stored at the 4-bit footprint. g15's 148 B was nominal, not measured.
- SSD-backed exact rerank (`FileRows`, direct I/O):
  - Cost: 70 µs per row single-threaded. A shared handle stays at 14k rows/s; one handle per thread scales to 113k rows/s at 8 threads.
  - What it buys: turbovec 4-bit with x4 rerank keeps 196-207 B RAM/vec (4.8-5.1 M/GB) at recall 0.999-1.000 up to N=1e6.
  - Latency cost: p50 5.7-6.2 ms at 3e5 (3.9 ms with 4 I/O handles) and 14.6 ms at 1e6, against 2.9 ms and 10 ms with the rows in RAM.
- HNSW with block-fp16 stored points (custom `Distance<i16>`) saves 10-18 % of bytes at equal recall and equal or lower latency. int8 points cap recall at 0.96-0.97, so I don't recommend them.
- The full 3-D Pareto (RAM bytes x recall x p99, RAM-only and SSD views) is in `results/h8_pareto_mem.md`.

**6. RaBitQ-style multi-bit codes**
- I implemented a std-only version. It is equal to or slightly below turbovec per code bit. At 1e6, 4-bit recall is 0.755 vs 0.772, and 0.997 vs 0.999 with x4 rerank.
- Its only advantage is real 3-bit packing: 148.6 B vs 207 B. The scan is 1.5-3x slower.
- The science report's expectation that it matters at 1e5-1e6 is not supported here.
- I caught and fixed a bug of mine first: the rotation seed equalled the data-generator seed.

**7. Scale and concurrency**
- Scale runs at N=1e5/3e5/1e6 are complete; the tables are in the board entry and `results/h8_scale.md`.
- HNSW (M32/efc100/ef32, no lock) scales 3.9x on 4 readers (4,657 to 18,349 qps, p50 flat ~200 µs).
- One concurrent inserter at ~2.3k inserts/s does not slow the readers.
- Two writer threads inserting 6,000 vectors during reads lost none, and recall@10 stayed 0.993.

**8. Size-gating rule (measured crossovers, in the board entry)**
- N <= ~5k: exact flat.
- 5k-10k: int8 scan plus f32 rerank, or HNSW.
- 10k to ~3.5e5 (2.5 GB RAM budget): HNSW M24-32, efc >= 3M, ef 16-24 (ef 64-128 at 1e5; M48/efc100 ef128-256 at 3e5).
- RAM-bound beyond that: turbovec 4-bit codes plus x4 exact rerank, with the f32 rows on SSD if bytes matter.
- Bytes-extreme: turbovec 2-bit with x16 rerank.

**Honest negatives**
- Peak working set at N=1e6 was 3.15 GB, over my 2.5 GB cap. Free RAM stayed above 5 GB and nothing paged.
- Single-build sweep points are noisy.
- No real corpus >= 1e5 exists, and the real sets are templated near-duplicates.
- Not measured: real mmap page-fault path, deletes, filtered search, more than 4 reader threads.
